posts.title: People who cured / are curing their own cancer on X
posts.author: Jeff Tang (@jefftangx)
posts.text:
People who cured / are curing their own cancer on X:

1/ @sytses - bone cancer, billionaire founder of Gitlab, developed 10+ personalized therapies for himself. 

2/ @paul_conyngham - shrank his dog Rosie's mast cell cancer tumors after chemo and surgery weren't enough. Now backed by YC and Founders Fund

3/ @miriamgonp - stage 4 breast cancer, tumor sequenced, searching for vaccine manufacturer now

4/ @kevinace - stage 4 lung cancer, angel investor in 300+ companies, first drug stopped working after 18 months. Vaccine designed, now paying $300k out of pocket for the vaccine

5/ @masonbgrant:  going founder mode on his his 32-year-old wife's rare liver cancer, sequencing her tumor with AI agents

6/ @ArunRLverma: former product leader at Atoms and Shopify, brain tumor, built a vaccine from his tumor. Now building an AI health agent startup based on what he went through

We're going to make it

posts.title: We’ve just made public 125,091 DICOM radiology images from across my cancer journey (lin…
posts.author: Sid Sijbrandij (@sytses)
posts.text:
We’ve just made public 125,091 DICOM radiology images from across my cancer journey (link below). The data is both longitudinal and multi-modal, dated and linked to my treatment timeline, so you can compare imaging across initial diagnosis, standard of care, first remission, “founder mode cancer care”, and second remission. It’s viewable in OHIF, the standard open-source viewer used in radiology research.

Given the long history of applying deep learning to radiology, we’re hoping to see a variety of methods and models applied to my data. If you find something interesting, please reach out to cancer@sytse.com, or if you know a researcher who should see this, tag them below.

Thanks to Terra LaFerriere for organizing these images, and Kamil Slowikowski for building http://osteosarc.com into the resource it is.
